title: Resource Analysis for Quantum Simulation of Spatially Varying Transport-Reaction Equations
authors: Benjamin Jasperson, Krishna Garikipati, Siddhartha Srivastava
abstract: Spatially varying coefficients are the primary source of circuit complexity in quantum simulation of linear advection-diffusion-reaction equations. This work presents a resource analysis of single-step quantum propagators constructed using sparse FABLE block encodings, Quantum Singular Value Transformation, and linear-combination-of-unitaries. We derive theoretical estimates for qubit count, gate complexity, and circuit depth in terms of the spatial discretization, sparsity, and polynomial degree, and compare these predictions with synthesized quantum circuits for one- and two-dimensional variable-coefficient problems. The resulting analysis quantifies the cost of encoding realistic transport operators and provides practical resource estimates for near-term implementations.
summary: This paper provides a detailed resource analysis for using quantum circuits to simulate PDEs with spatially varying coefficients. It quantifies the qubit count and gate complexity required, showing that while theoretically possible, high accuracy demands an extremely deep circuit depth. The findings guide researchers toward using approximate encoding techniques to make such simulations feasible on current hardware.
main_problem: The work quantifies the computational resources (qubit count, gate complexity, circuit depth) needed to simulate linear advection-diffusion-reaction equations when coefficients vary spatially.
main_result: The resource cost scales linearly with spatial qubits, and maintaining high accuracy requires a very large number of native gates ($10^5–10^6$), suggesting that approximate block encodings are necessary for near-term feasibility.
method: It uses quantum algorithms like Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) combined with Sparse-FABLE block encodings to implement the time evolution operator derived from a Lie product splitting of the PDE.
model_or_system: The system is governed by a linear advection-diffusion-reaction equation on a periodic domain, discretized into a semi-discrete matrix form ($d|c(t)angle/dt = A |c(t)angle$).
key_observables: Qubit count ($n_{	ext{qubits}}$), gate complexity, circuit depth, and final state infidelity.
important_parameters: Spatial discretization size ($d$), sparsity structure of the coefficients, polynomial degree ($r$) used in QSVT, and time step ($\Delta t$).
main_assumptions: Assumes smooth and periodic coefficient fields; uses Gershgorin's theorem bounds for spectral norm estimation; relies on Lie product splitting and QSVT approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the scaling of single-step gate counts versus problem size (N) for 1D/2D simulations. Figure 2 illustrates how polynomial degree ($r$) and time step ($\Delta t$) affect final state infidelity in a 2D system.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical resource estimates based on block encodings, analyzes the error sources from Lie splitting and QSVT approximation, and compares these theoretical bounds with scaling predictions for 1D/2D problems.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical implementation challenges of simulating complex physical dynamics (like those found in AMO or open quantum systems) on near-term quantum hardware by providing concrete resource estimates.
